utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The witness -- Your Honour, before I turn over this witness for cross, may I just take --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's on but it's not working. The green light is flashing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a loud voice so maybe my voice--

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphones are working.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- will be picked up. The microphones are out on the Prosecution side of the table. When we press them we get a flashing green light but with the red light indicating the microphone is on but they're not working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Maybe they'll return when you're ready to re-examine. But yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I failed to admit one of the exhibits that was admitted in the Vasiljevic case through the transcript. It was -- it's our 65 ter number 91 and it was Exhibit number 66 in the Vasiljevic case. I would just like that to be admitted along with the transcripts since this is a --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is not working so we cannot interpret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And before we begin the court deputy also has an announcement to make.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would like to make a correction to Friday's --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the registrar. The interpreters can't interpret if they can't hear the speakers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would like to make a correction for Friday's transcript. Exhibit P80 admitted under seal, the pseudonym sheet for the witness, will become Exhibit P84 under seal. And 65 ter number 91 will become Exhibit P85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Alarid, your turn to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I still don't have a microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There seems to be a technical problem. We need a break of five minutes, so we'll just stay here. I think we should just stay for five minutes and exercise some patience. It's now working.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I believe mine's on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. VG-18. I apologise that we weren't able to get to you on Friday and I know that it's hard for you probably to stay here away from your home and family for this long, especially under such stressful circumstances, and I apologise for keeping you. We left a little early on Friday because this was so stressful for you. Are you okay today? And, ma'am, I see that you're nodding, but I don't think -- we do need to speak in the microphone for the interpreter if we could.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll stick it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. Thank you. I appreciate your patience and your strength with this. Now, at first I'd like to question you about your earliest statements that you gave after this incident. Can we talk about that first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, there's -- in our research in all the documents that the Prosecution has given us, they gave us a statement that did not bear your signature in any way, but it was published in Naser Oric's book related to the genocide in Visegrad. Have you ever seen this book or heard of this book?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. Wherever -- whatever doesn't bear my signature I will not discuss that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's fair enough, ma'am. I just note that it had a date of interviews taken regarding the fire at Pionirska Street as 11 September 1992, and I just wonder if you remember being questioned about this tragedy as early as September of that year.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was anyone from Srebrenica. I don't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you do recall giving a statement in the 17th of May, 1993, to the security services in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what -- how did it come to be that you would give a statement as a witness to this crime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got out of Srebrenica as an infirm person. I was exhausted. It was in Banovici that they called me up, and I told them the story about how I got there and where I got there from. I told them that I was so exhausted when I reached Banovici that I was unable to get off the truck myself. That's how it was. And they called those other people to ask me about that story, though I was too exhausted to talk much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long were you able to speak with them when you spoke with these investigators in 1993? May 17th, to be specific.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Half an hour to an hour. I don't know exactly. I only gave them the story -- an outline of the story, I was so exhausted. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please approach the microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, you need to sit closer to the microphone. The interpreter is having a hard time hearing you. Now, in your statement of 1993, you started out by speaking about how the situation got worse and how it got started. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember everything. I will stop remembering only when I die. That was where my life ended. My family and I no longer are alive, and I will tell you everything I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: For how many generations did your family live in Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Can you please explain your question. How many generations? I got married into -- into that village. I didn't live there before. I wouldn't be able to tell you that exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well -- and a family name of the victims was many of the same family name, the Kurspahic family, and maybe that's what I meant in terms of how many generations that family had been there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, that. I understand. I understand. There were two, in my household there were three, five, four. I only know that in the Memisevic household there were two. And there was one Kurspahic who only lived with his wife. Otherwise, the families numbered four, five, six members. Two families had a home in Visegrad, and they went to join their children over there earlier on and they survived. Other families that resided in the village are no longer among the living.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. And I'm going to try and not interrupt you, but we have to have a question and answer time, okay? So would it be fair to say that the Kurspahic family had lived there for many, many years going back several generations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes. For instance, my grand grandfather had five sons, and they all had houses in the neighbourhood, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I noticed that in your first statement you noted that there were small villages or hamlets around your village, including a village called Gavrilovici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our village was called Koritnik, and the Serb part of the village was also called Koritnik. They were our neighbours. We lived together.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So these -- all these names are just neighbourhoods or little areas in the same village, to understand you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was called Koritnik, and Serbs and Muslims lived there. There is Ubava, Greben, Prelovo. These are villages a bit further off. In our village Muslims and Serbs lived together side by side.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that you believe that the surrounding villages, the Serbians received their ammunition and weapons from the JNA when they were in town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Uzice Corps, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at the same time the Uzice Corps took away the most basic weapons of your family members and your people, even to hunt and feed themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything had been taken from us, but not many had weapons. Maybe two or three men had hunting rifles. Had we known that they would attack us, we would have tried and obtained weapons. As it was, we did not. We did not think we had any need for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Because you and your people lived a simple life of farming and taking care of your families?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Farm work. My husband spent some five years in Austria on his own. I stayed behind with children. We had fertile land, and together with the Visegrad cooperative we had cows. I managed to earn my living and school my children based on the milk the cows yielded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your statement of 1993, you indicated that your husband saw your neighbour Dusan Grujic's cellar packed with ammunition and rockets and grenades and other ammunition?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gavrilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is that Dragomir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That house was closest to ours. He went over to Dusan's and was able to see that. They were hiding it in the other room. Milana must have entered the room and opened the door, and he saw that a corner of the room had been full of arms. In the evening they brought over a small TAM, and we could hear them load some of the weapons at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that it was the SDS party that started the extremism against Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not against us. I don't want to go into politics. As far as our Serbs were concerned, they did tell us that we had to leave, but it was not their own initiative. Dragomir did come and threaten, but he did not have a say-so. He was on the police force, but he wasn't the one issuing orders. As far as my neighbours are concerned and my family's concerned, we were not mistreated. They only came on one occasion and told us that we were supposed to surrender weapons or else be killed. I said that we didn't have weapons. But it was just him. He was the one who came asking for the weapons. Others did not mistreat me or my family. I cannot speak for the rest of the village though. I avoided attending any meetings, and I avoided being asked questions. I wanted to protect my children. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this particular individual in terms of somebody coming over to mistreat us, nothing of the sort happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that Drago was a member of the Crisis Stab?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about that. I didn't know about such-and-such person being of that sort or another, of this ilk or another. I didn't know of the SDS, of the staffs. I wasn't interested in anything. They -- I didn't benefit from their existence in any way. I'm not a politician.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But in your 1993 statement you did talk about the politics, the SDS, and the Crisis Stab, and you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, fine. Of course, the whole world knew that there were these parties, the SDA and SDS, that they were nationalist. If I did say that they were nationalist, I didn't mean that I experienced that. I lived on my homestead and was not interested in them. Even if it's called the Serb Republic nowadays, I still go to see my house in Visegrad. I'm not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And another police officer was involved in removing you from your home, and that was Ilija Gavrilovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he may have been there. I heard stories to that effect. But he didn't tell me that I should leave. There was only one Radomir Djuric who came to visit us and tell us that we ought to leave. I don't know if he was on the military police or not. Ilija, on the other hand, did not tell me anything. I can only speak for myself and my child. I do not want to impute anything to anyone that I am not certain of.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And your village was attacked in very early April by the Gavrilovics and other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Tell us about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know about that. I went over to Dusan's, to his garage to where his son lived, and that's where I spent the night because I did not dare to sleep at home. My husband slept at our house, and in the morning he came over and said, "Let's get away. All of them have left. There are no Serbs around. They are about to attack us. Let us get out of the village. They could have killed last night but they didn't, so we should leave." As I left down toward the Drina I heard shots fired upon our village. We fled across the Drina and into a forest where we hid. I left the keys to my home to my neighbours, and asked them to tend my livestock.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it was in between this attack by these people on your village and the tragedy with the fire that the Uzice Corps came into town. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you remember being herded into the football stadium to hear from a General Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything. I remember everything. I remember that Sepo came over. He was talking over a megaphone telling us that we could go to Visegrad and beyond if we wanted to. My husband was with me. We had spent the night in the forest, and as we got out of the forest we came across an army. It was the Uzice Corps. They escorted us to the station in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that General Jovanovic told the crowd of Muslims that the White Eagles were under his control?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course he did. There were a lot of people gathered there. You couldn't even hear well everything that he was saying because of the crowd. He sent people around to go and search for those who were hiding, and then he noticed us and got down and approached us to see what had become of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that you noticed White Eagles around the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were ordinary people. I don't know what they were called. They were just regular soldiers with multicoloured uniforms. What they were called, the White Eagles or the Uzice Corps, I don't know. They were an army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that you heard from people coming to your village that even as the Uzice Corps was in town, the White Eagles were taking the young men, the young Muslim men, and making them gone missing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. From my village, and I can list them even now. They were men aged 30, Hidajet Kurspahic, Osman Kurspahic, Fikret Kurspahic. He was a soldier in Belgrade. Omer Kurspahic and his son Almir. He may have been 12 years of age at the time. They all went missing and their fate is still unknown, including this child aged 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to take you forward a little bit to around the 12th of June, 1992. Do you remember a Serbian police officer named Radomir Djuric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was he the first policeman to come to your town and tell you you had to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some went to attend the negotiations in Prelovo. There was one person there we called Micun. I don't know what his family name is. Lipovac, I believe. He was the first one to come over with a couple of soldiers wearing that Seselj's cockade on his head and asked, "Where is your husband?" I told him that he had gone to tend the cattle. And then I asked him, "Why do you need him -- what do you need him for?" Answer, "I need him because I want him to go to Prelovo." I offered to go instead and he said no, call Osman Kurspahic and Nedjo Memisevic. I want them to go there because I have the time to. I called the two men and they went to the local commune in Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, also is that when Dragomir Gavrilovic came to your home as well, the next -- was that the next day? He had asked about a machine-gun and your husband's whereabouts, and he wanted to know where the gun was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And then -- so when was it that Ilija and Dragomir came to the home and said everyone had to leave on the buses? Was that on the 13th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Radomir came from Loznica and said that we had to leave on Sunday at 7.00, that we had to be by the bus station to go to Kladanj or Olovo and that we were to take some food with us and two changes of clothes and food for a day or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you were walking from your homes to Visegrad, did you encounter other police officers to escort you on your way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, without your question can I say this first: When we set off my husband didn't want to go with us because he knew -- in the previous war his father told him that if you took to the woods you survived. So he didn't want to go with us. We went to Dusan and told him to tell him to go down with the others to the meeting point, and so that's how we left, and he set off with us. He accompanied us to Greben, to the ridge, but there were no buses so we had to wait there until 10.00, and then he went to call Micun, and Micun took us to Banja. I don't know. Or Sase.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, my case manager indicated there was a point in there where she used her name. There may need to be a redaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what was the first time you saw Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I went with my children, of course, with my daughter. She worked nearby, and so I went to the new hotel. But I didn't know him. I didn't know him. I don't remember him. I know his -- Milojkas, he worked with us, but I didn't know him until he came up there where we were supposed to be put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your statement of 1993 you made several corrections of which we talked about -- or the Prosecutor talked about at the beginning of Friday. What occurred in between 1998 and giving your testimony in 2001 that would cause you to remember things or clarify things?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't ask this witness anything about the 1993 statement, only about her statement to the ICTY Prosecutors, so I think Mr. Alarid --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm simply looking at the proofing report filed on Friday in this case and it notes that there were some corrections to the 17 May 1993 statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, okay, but your question was in your statement of 1998 you made several corrections that the Prosecutor talked about at the beginning of Friday, so I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would like to focus first on your 1993 statement. You made several corrections, having read that. Did you read your statement all the way through, the 1993 one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I don't know. I mix up Milan and whatever. Maybe I did. But as far as adding more things, well, I didn't add anything if I didn't leave anything out. Maybe I mixed their names up, because I don't know who's who even now. So I might have mixed the two of them up. I didn't know them from earlier on, and I hadn't seen them, so maybe I mixed that up. They introduced themselves and said Mitar Vasiljevic and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, in just reading the statement of 1993, I noted that you never mentioned Milan Lukic in the entire statement when I first read it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well- that’s- I give that- I mean- I apologise. Perhaps that is the case- that I- I don’t know. Because- because always- your wits are not- you get nervous- that’s perhaps how I… But to my mind, Milan was a bit stouter than Sredoje- I don’t know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have lost the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, can we get the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, you're going to need to repeat yourself only because the interpretation did not come through, and so I could not hear your answer. Can you -- can you say why you had made that mistake?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately we haven't got translation in B/C/S now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now we have it in B/C/S. Thank you. I apologise for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, what I had basically asked you is did you realise that you never mentioned Milan Lukic in the entire statement that you gave in 1993, and I think you gave an explanation as to why that was the case.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Really, I- I’m wondering myself how come I didn't mention him, but the person doing the interpretation got something wrong and the one questioning me. I don’t really know how come everything I said was about Sredoje and that’s not how it was. So I apologise, if you can accept that, and if not, well, I don’t know. Because I am not always- sometimes I’m a bit nervous, somebody comes to ask me something and- and I am all- it cannot come back and I have to do it. That’s how it is maybe, I don’t know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in your proofing statement you now made the change Mitar to Milan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Mitar. I didn't see Mitar any more. He was there once, but maybe he was with them, but I don't know. I didn't see him. I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When did you stop seeing Mitar that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I said who came. That might have been what I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in -- also you made a correction that originally you thought the person you knew as Sredoje came with a brother, and now you said in your proofing statement that you know they are not brothers. How did you come to that realisation between when you had testified earlier, given statements earlier, to today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is how I changed my statement: I perhaps thought that they were brothers because they were both Lukic. That's why I thought they were brothers. They were together. Now, later on I learnt that they weren't brothers and that they were cousins. Just like brothers, in fact, first cousins.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did you -- who told you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know who told me. How should I know? I heard it said, but I don't know. I can't say exactly who I heard it from. So can I first say -- if I may be allowed to say first that Sredoje's wife worked with my daughter, so she knows. So she found it strange. They worked together, I know that, so I can state that now, here and now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But on the night you gave -- or the time you gave the statement in 1993, you believed they were brothers, even if you were mistaken? And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you indicated that they're --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That the brother had a skinny cropped beard and now you say his nickname was Lalco. But it sounded in the statement like one of the people you thought to be Lukic had a beard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This one, the one that was at Greben, at the ridge, had a small beard. I didn't say that the others had beards, neither one of them. One of them had this pointy face and chin, but as for the others, I didn't say that about them. That's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Still, were they both clean-shaven then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I saw, yes, they did. How other people saw them, I don't know. I didn't really look at them. I was just looking at my child and seeing to my own affairs. I didn't look round at anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you also corrected it to say that neither Lukic ordered women to strip naked. That was someone else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, whether anybody ordered it or not, they said that we would go into the room two by two, and Milan said that we would go into their room and that they would strip us naked, take our clothes off. Now, whether he ordered it or not, I don't know. When I was in the room and took my clothes off, this young man -- well, it wasn't either one of these. Now, whether they came in later on or not, I don't know. All I do know is what I told you in the statement, what I went through and experienced.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, when you say it was not either one of these two, is that not either one of these two gentlemen sitting in court today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes, yes. When I was there, when I was over there inside that room and when I came out, I came out in a terrible state. I heard my child crying on the other side of the door, and I don't remember anything. I don't know who dragged me in or dragged me out or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'm going to move on but so I don't forget, I would like to tender the statement of this witness given in 17 May 1993, which has been uploaded as 1D10-0417, and the B/C/S version has been uploaded as 1D10-0425.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as 1D33 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you then next gave a statement in the 17th of January, 1995. Do you remember that? Do you remember that, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And there's a -- I apologise, Your Honour. On the B/C/S version, of course the one signed by the witness, it's on the 27th of January, whereas the English translation has the 17th of January, and that must be a typographical error.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, did you have an opportunity to read your 1995 statement in advance of your testimony as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Why should I read it when I know everything, but yes, I did read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I mean would it be fair to say that you memory should be better closer to the incident that you were reporting on than, of course, several years later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll answer your question. I know everything. Yes, everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your 1995 statement you stated that Dragomir Gavrilovic also came to your village and threatened to kill you, and in that statement you say that Milan Lukic was there and Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Who said that? No, I never saw these people in my village ever. No, I didn't say that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I apologise, ma'am. I really only meant Dragomir Gavrilovic from your village is now at the scene of the fire in your 1995 statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think if -- if counsel is going to be questioning the witness about her prior statements perhaps he should put them up on the screen and let her see the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Certainly. Could we call up what's been uploaded as 1D10-0432, and the B/C/S version is 1D10-0436. And I'm going to go to page 3 of the English version, focusing on the third paragraph. And it's also going to be page 3 of the B/C/S version, second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: While this is coming on the screen I would just ask the Court to ask Defence counsel to please put this in context of date because the date is not mentioned on this page, if he would.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid, do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, the reference from page 2 is: "The following day, 14 June 1994."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'd like you to look down at your statement. I know it's a little bit fuzzy from the age, but at the paragraph where it says "2300" at the beginning of the first sentence. And I see Dragomir Gavrilovic's name about three or four sentences down. Have you had -- have you had a chance to read that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Go ahead and ask your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that the electricity was out in the Memic house? There was no electricity or lights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some electricity from the other houses, because it was one house next to another. So you could see. But I don't know, inside, no, there wasn't. Well, I don't know. No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the sentence starts out with someone told you basically to leave your things and you could pick them up in the morning, and you said, "Since it was dark I could not see the face of this man, but I recognised the voices as those of Sredoje Lukic, who was in the company of Milan Lukic and Dragomir Gavrilovic, who earlier in the village had threatened to kill us."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes. When they came, that person -- well, it was one of the two. I didn't look. I can't tell you the details. There was general panic and the house was full, full of us people. So I just looked -- took care of my child. I didn't look around. But I heard from others, and what I saw was when somebody in uniform came to the door, and in the morning when they took the money and gold, judging by the voice, but I wasn't close to see -- close by to say -- and I didn't say Dragomir Gavrilovic. Well, he didn't come to the house. He was down there, Dragomir Gavrilovic. He wasn't in the house. I don't exclude the possibility of him being down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And down there, down where, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where they said we had to go to Adem Omeragic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now you say there was a man at the door in a uniform. Can you describe the uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a camouflage uniform, I think, but I really don't know, I can't say for sure. There were a lot of people and I didn't look around. I wasn't interested in uniforms, so don't bother me with that kind of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How much --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, the Prosecution had an hour and 15 minutes, and that period of time will be what is allotted to you, and it will be up at 1.45 when we take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, did you -- did you notice what Mitar Vasiljevic was wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did. I saw him arrive when we were there in front of the house. He had a coat of some kind, a black one, and a hat, and a feather in his hat. I didn't notice anything else. I didn't really look, to tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the person that you believed to be Milan Lukic, what was he wearing? Because -- because you'd never met him before that night; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day Mitar Vasiljevic put us up -- put us there. We didn't see him, but when he came at 5.00 to take up the money and the gold, before that time, before the time you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And let's go to 5.00, then, and other people arrived. Can you tell me what they are wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes. They came then, and then they came to tell us to go down to that other house. You keep asking me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, ma'am. I just want you to go into your memory and describe to me what these men were wearing. Now, you've explained Mitar Vasiljevic. Now let's move on with other people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones that came had automatics, nothing else. What else would they have? I didn't see anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What kind of clothes did they have had on? And were they wearing different clothes or were they wearing all the same clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two of them were wearing the same, but Mitar Vasiljevic wasn't wearing a uniform at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you still assert that Mitar Vasiljevic was there at 11.00 or midnight the night of the fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they can say that. They didn't know we were there until somebody told them. I never saw these guys, these young guys either on the way or anything. So either Dragomir Gavrilovic told them, or Vasiljevic told them, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And these guys, what were they wearing? How many of them were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one that came to the door, of course he was in uniform. It was probably one of the two of them, whether it was Milan or Sredoje. Maybe I would know if I looked at them, but I didn't look at them, of course because I was busy waking up my child, and I had problems with my child who was ill. But judging by the voice, I recognised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it possible that different men or more men came than were there earlier in the night when you were humiliated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came -- others came and took people off to dig trenches, the victims. Four of our menfolk went, but they returned as well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: To dig graves. Interpreter's correction, to dig graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm more interested in the soldiers that came around midnight and asked you to move from one house to the other. I'm more interested in how many came, how many, and what they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just told you. There was one person in uniform. I saw that, but I know nothing more. Judging by the voices, I thought it was either Milan or Sredoje. Let's say Milan, that they had come. Now, how many of them there were outside, I don't know, because only one of them came in. I'm sure there were more of them outside because you could hear them talking and laughing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I would like to introduce the January 1995 statements both in B/C/S and English that have already been identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They will be admitted as 1D34 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then the next time you gave a statement was the 4th of February in 1998, and that was to the International Criminal Tribunal. Do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you recall how you came to be asked to give a statement for the international court? Because clearly you were giving statements to your local authorities before, but now you're dealing with the international authorities.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, truth to tell. I do remember giving statements. I may have left something out or it can be corrected. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you did not correct the part of your 1998 statement that said that you saw many White Eagles there at the stadium, and you stated in there that you believed that the White Eagles and the Uzice Corps were the same unit. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they were the same unit or not. How should I know who the White Eagles or the Uzice Corps were? I only knew that they were an army. Where they had come from, if they were Serbs -- please don't go on bothering me with these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I hope to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll just ask you to be patient, Witness, and we'll finish with your evidence shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, yes, ma'am, I'm only going to ask you a few more questions, okay? Now, in the proofing notes that were filed with this case, in your statement originally you stated that Milan Lukic was about 35 years old. That is what she thought at the time. Was the age of Milan Lukic discussed in the proofing session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. By God I don't know. What I said about the age that he had, I stand by that. I probably judged his age by what I saw, on the basis of his appearance at the time. This is something that I said, and they might have asked me to give his age roughly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, the person that you believed to be Milan Lukic, can you tell me what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just as every other soldier. He was no different from others. He had boots on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us hear Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting but we missed something in the transcript. Page 24, line 24. The witness explained that she didn't know the age of Sredoje Lukic. We can clarify with additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll clarify if you'd like, Djuro, because that was my next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, in your statement the person that you had believed to be Sredoje Lukic you thought was 40 years old at the time. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was giving statements on this issue, they said that it didn't matter exactly what his age was, that I should give the approximate age, and I did so. I wasn't there when they were born to know their exact age. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were they wearing anything on their heads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see. I think that they had those military caps. Maybe they had them behind their belts, but I did seem to recall them not having anything on their heads. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you believed that Dragomir Gavrilovic was on duty that night. Do you mean as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. As we were on the move, my husband went over to ask Dusan to accompany us on our way. Dusan said, "But you're safe." So I know that he worked that evening. I'm not sure whether he was on duty when he was -- during the night. I only know about when my husband went over to ask him to escort us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you also felt he knew where you and your family was that night; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean at my house or down there when we got there? I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Down there at the Memic house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course he knew. When we were just below our village, there was our neighbour Hamizalija, that he got there and then went to town together with Ilija. He took a car and he waved out of the car towards us that we should go down there, and the other one was telling him to stop waving to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so it was like he knew where you had to go before you were even told to go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that he knew that. They should be the ones to investigate that. First of all, there was no bus waiting for us there at 7.00 as it should have been. Second, did he know about where they were taking us? Did he tell them to take us there and do to us what they did? I don't know. As soon as I realised that no buses were forthcoming, I knew that something was brewing. I mean, this isn't any sort of information that I got. I simply felt this when I saw that no buses arrived, I realised that they were lying us to. The man from Loznica, he said that there would be a bus waiting for us and that even our police force would be escorting us to our destination to make sure that we are safe. Now, these men should be the ones to investigate who it was who ordered them to do that to us. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so wouldn't it be fair to say that the people that profited the most from you leaving your village, the people that took your land afterwards might be the ones that also planned your exodus?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. It calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you've --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You've also asked two questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. I can't say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on. She can't answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, the 1998 statement was already introduced as P83, and at this point in time we -- but we would like to introduce the proofing notes. 1D10-1626.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. The proofing notes are notes from the attorneys, the attorney's recollection of notes that the attorney made at the proofing session. These were not read by the witness. They're not signed by the witness. They're attorney notes. They're not evidence, notes that are passed along to the Defence as a courtesy. They're not evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think -- you know, part of the problems with 92 ter and these large statements coming in with only the right to cross-examine is some of the corrections are coming from these meetings, and one thing that I think is going to be relevant over time and if we have to make it part of a submission as opposed to evidence and put it in an annex, maybe that's the way to move the point, but all these proofing statements are causing minor shifts in the testimony either by name, description, or date, and I think that that's going to become apparent over the course of time. And like I said, I think the witness has already testified to some of these factors of which may speak for themselves but obviously the typewritten English is a little sometimes maybe more on point than the testimony we've gotten, since the witness tends to answer in the narrative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see Mr. Groome is on his feet. What are these proofing notes? How are they made?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, they're generated, Your Honour, when a witness comes to testify in The Hague. And in preparation for their testimony the attorneys provide them with their older statements and may ask them additional questions. When they provide information which is not contained in their previous statements, it's the Prosecutor's position that we should be disclosing this, and the mechanism that we use for disclosing anything in addition that the witness has provided or anything that may be different is the proofing note. I would very much oppose that it is given the same status as a witness statement, but may I make a suggestion with respect to how it's been dealt with in other cases, and perhaps it might be a way that it be dealt with here. I believe the matter that's contained in the proofing note could be put to the witness. Did you not say yesterday or whatever date's on the proofing note, did you not say to the Prosecutor X, Y, and Z. Depending what the witness says, the Prosecution afterward would be willing to enter into a stipulation or an agreement that on the date indicated in the proofing note, that was in fact said to the Prosecutor handling the case, and that way we would avoid giving these proofing -- these notes which are essentially notes generated by an attorney and attributing them to the witness but still Mr. Cepic and Mr. Alarid would have the benefit of evidence on the record that the Prosecution agrees that the witness did make such a statement the day or whatever day's indicated on the proofing note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, my own mind isn't made up on it, but my brother and my sister are against its admission, so we won't admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could revisit it, Your Honour, as long as we have the -- as long as we have the proofing note uploaded, we might be able to make a further submission at the end. It's just sometimes difficult to cross-examine the witness in this way, especially since there are so many statements that have come in. It's extremely difficult to cross-examine the statements when these witnesses are, one, so stressed over their testimony and their answers tend to be narrative. This does indicate that there are these minor changes that I think doesn't go to the admissibility but to the weight of the evidence. I think what it really is going to hinge on is the weight you give it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move only. Let's move on, Mr. Alarid. I've already given the ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Then I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sartorio -- sorry, I mean Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I do have some questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. You are allowed to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Let me first introduce myself to you. My name is Djuro Cepic, and I represent the Defence for Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Before I put my first question to you, let me tell you this: I understand the pain and the suffering your son and you experienced during this incident. On behalf of my team and in my name, I wish to express my sympathy for what you and your son have suffered during that incident. Please listen to my questions carefully so that we can go through them quickly. Can you please repeat your answer? It was not recorded in the transcript. Do you understand what I said to you so far?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I represent the Defence for Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that. That I know. I understand everything. Please go ahead with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam, I put it to you that Sredoje Lukic, who is seated in this courtroom here today, did not take part in this incident because on that day he was a long way away from Visegrad. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't understand that. That's not true at all. I have not come here at the age of 67 to tell lies or to impute things that the person has not done.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Your child, VG-84, was it with you throughout the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the war, and it's still with me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were VG-13 and VG-38 with you throughout the incident, at all times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Hasib Kurspahic was there with you as well, was he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Following this incident, at a later date, you, your son, VG-84, and Edhem Kurspahic were refugees in Srebrenica, were you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You'll agree with me that neither your son, VG-84, nor Edhem Kurspahic, nor you knew Sredoje Lukic before this incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I wouldn't even know them today. Just -- if they had not introduced themselves to me, if they had not said that they were Milan or Sredoje Lukic. I would not be able to tell you about him -- about them. And this is true for everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I understand. Edhem Kurspahic and your son didn't know who is who before this incident, before these men introduced themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Edhem knew only Lalco, that he was… he told us that this was him. He 17 said, how come that thug joined ranks with them. He used to plough his land…

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I was going object to the question asking what other people knew, if -- I guess he could lay a foundation whether she knows whether they knew or not. The question was Edhem Kurspahic and your son didn't know who is who before this incident. I'm not sure she can speak for them. It's a speculative -- it calls for a speculative answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, can you answer the question whether Edhem Kurspahic and your son didn't know who before the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't know them before. They got to know them, just as I did, when they came to Mujo Memic's house and introduced themselves to us. Well, I didn't know about Edhem, but my son didn't know them. How could he have known them? There's no speculation in that, I'm sure. He definitely did not know them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, not all of your words were interpreted. You said that Edhem only recognised Lalco. Did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And the others he didn't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the others he knew him just as I did, when they introduced themselves, and this is true for my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could I have in e-court system Exhibit number P83, seventh page in B/C/S and seventh page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, let us look at your 1998 statement briefly. This is a statement you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. You are the same age as my mother, and she has quite poor eyesight. Are you able to read what you can see on the screen here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't make out what I can see on the screen. I don't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to read this out to you, and you can then just look and see if this is exactly what it says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'll hear what you have to say and then I'll tell you if it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In paragraph two it says, line two: "As they got into the house they were Milan Lukic, Sredoje Lukic, and Laco. Sredoje Lukic said that he was Sredoje Lukic." "The other two were recognised by other people in the room." Do you recall this part your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I know at all times that they had introduced themselves as Sredoje and Milan. I have nothing else to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have P82. In e-court system page 29. This is the transcript of testimony of this witness in the case against Mitar Vasiljevic, page number 1581. I need bottom of the page, from 19th line. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, this is the transcript of your testimony in the Mitar Vasiljevic case. Colleague Groome asked us, starting on line 19: "I'm asking you about the man that came to the house after Mitar Vasiljevic gave you the certificate. How many men came to the house at that time?" Your answer was: "People came. Sredoje Lukic came with the people. He introduced himself. I wouldn't have recognised him, but he introduced himself ..." Now, I'd like to know the following, madam: During your testimony on Friday in answer to the Prosecutor's question, you gave a statement that was noticeably different on this particular issue, and you said that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Sartorio is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we see the question that was put to the witness on Friday, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the answer too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I have to find just this part of the transcript from Friday, which is inclusion with -- in the previous testimony. May I complete the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you may complete it, but for our purposes Ms. Sartorio I think is correct. It would be very helpful to see the question that was put on Friday and the answer which you say was noticeably different.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The page number is 1303, lines from 8 to 17th. If it's possible to have this page in front us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the age of technology it should.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: 1303, please. Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I have some assistance with my screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just note that it is the time that you had said you wanted to break. If there's a technical problem, perhaps would it be wise to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take the adjournment now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, I left off looking at your transcript of Friday, page 1303, and with regards to this, who introduced himself or whatever, you said on line 13: "They came. Milan Lukic said that his name was Milan Lukic, and the other one said that he was Sredoje Lukic. As for the third one, I didn't hear anything until they had gone." Madam, I'm asking you now, did somebody perhaps tell you what you were supposed to say before this court here today when testifying? Did they suggest anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am testifying to the best of my recollections everything that I lived through. I gave statements about what I had lived through and experienced.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we have P82, page in e-court system 70, 7-0. It is the page 1622 from the Vasiljevic trial. Let me see the page number in the upper corner. Thank you. Could you scroll down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, my colleague Mr. Domazet asked you a question, and your answer was as follows, this was in a previous trial, the trial of Mitar Vasiljevic: "I wouldn't know Mitar either had he not said who he was. I wouldn't have known him either, been able to recognise him. And I would have said the same about him as I did about the they other men. I didn't know them." And then line 20 where you say: "I didn't know them. This Milan came and said that he was Sredoje Lukic and that is how I know." And that's lines 20 and 21 of the transcript. Now, what I'm interested in is this: Did Milan Lukic say that he was Sredoje Lukic, or did he indicate, point to somebody else, point to another man and introduced that man to the other people and said, "This man is Sredoje Lukic"? Which was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how are you asking me that? I've said any number of times that I was in a group of people and that I just heard who said what. I didn't look around who was Milan, who was Sredoje. So I'm looking at them now and I don't really know. I can't say. I can't recognise which is which or who is who. I just heard people saying in that group of people that one of these men was Milan Lukic and that the other was Sredoje Lukic, and had they not introduced themselves, well, I wouldn't have even have known their names, but they gave their names themselves. So don't tire me with that any longer. I'm not a fortune-teller to know whether this one's Milan and that one's Sredoje.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I understand perfectly, madam, and I understand the pain and suffering you must be feeling. I'd just like you to help me out so we can clarify things to the best of your recollections, of course. Can you remember the moment when a person introduced themselves in the house and said, "I am Sredoje Lukic"? Can you remember that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course I can. We've just talked about it. Of course. How wouldn't I be able to remember? You just asked me and I answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I heard the testimony of VG-38, and he said that that Sredoje Lukic, that man, Sredoje Lukic, was lower in height than -- shorter in height than Milan Lukic, that he was five centimetres shorter, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. Is there a question before the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm just confronting the person. Could I complete the question, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is there anything to be redacted, Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: My colleague who does speak Bosnian said she did mention the name of one of the protected witnesses, but it's not in our English version. It doesn't -- it doesn't show up in the English transcript. It was just heard in the Bosnian. Yes. It was around line 37, I mean page 37, line 20, 20 to 24. Somewhere in there was the name of a person mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. The court deputy will deal with that. Continue, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have page from Friday 1304, 1304 page. Thank you. Scroll up a little bit just to see the last of previous page. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lines 4 and 5. You said that you weren't looking towards Sredoje and Milan, weren't looking at them. May I then conclude that you weren't looking towards that man when he introduced himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I would have looked had I been nearby, but I was in the room. They went into the general sitting area first. I just heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So you didn't actually see him when he introduced himself. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him, but when we went into another room, we all had to go to this other room, then I saw them, but I didn't know who was who.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, when you saw him then, I'd like to hear some details about what that person looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have 1D33 in the system of e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try and remind you by using your previous statements when describing that person as to have as much detail as possible. Madam, this is the statement that my colleague Alarid asked you about. It was given on the 17th of May, 1993, to the state security sector, Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have page 5 bottom of the page, and in B/C/S fourth page, also bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see your signature there on that statement, madam?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So just up above the signature it says, and I'll read it out. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not really, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'll read it out then. "At around 1700 hours, Sredoje Lukic came to the house, a retired policeman, as well as his brother and two other men." Madam, I'm interested in knowing the following: Where did you get the information that Sredoje Lukic was retired at the time? Who provided you with that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that, but I heard stories going round that he was in the police. His father told us with Huso. I know that the other one was a little shorter and darker skinned, whereas Milan had lighter skin. That's as far as I know. And I had heard that Hasim said that he was in the police force, this man Sredoje Lukic, but I didn't know him. I went to Visegrad, but I don't remember. I don't remember having anything to do with the police ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you don't remember the source. In light of what it says here in your statement, that man should be around Huso's age or maybe a little older; right? Can you tell us, is he -- was he about Huso's age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can we identify who Huso is? And also, if this is a protected witness, should this not be on the record?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Lay some foundation, Mr. Cepic. Is Huso a protected witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: He's not protected. He testified without any measure, as far as I can remember. My learned friends from OTP can remind me, but it was VG-61, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He's not a protected witness, I'm informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just wasn't sure who he was referring to, as he only said the first name. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, you know Huso Kurspahic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This man Sredoje who appeared in the house, was he about Huso's age, because you said that he was retired? Or was he older than Huso, perhaps younger than Huso?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really can't say. I don't know. I've said umpteen times that I didn't look at them, so please believe me. Now you want me to measure him up with someone else 17 years on. I really can't do that. I don't know. Just my story. Whether he was Huso's colleague or superior to him or his age or not, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When that man introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic at that moment, how far were they -- were VG-13 and VG-38 from where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we women were in the room, and the menfolk, when they arrived, were at the entrance to the sitting room. We were all there, but we -- all we were doing was following orders. We didn't look to see how old they were or what their date of birth was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In that group of women, the women who were with you, was VG-13 among them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, last week in this same courtroom before this same Trial Chamber we heard testimony from VG-13, and she said that she knew Sredoje Lukic and that she did not see him --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This line of questioning putting another -- statement from another witness to this witness isn't proper questioning. You can put the proposition to the witness but not confront this witness with what another witness has stated. This has happened on numerous occasions in the courtroom and it's objectionable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Trial Chambers will view this differently, but it's preferable to put the proposition, Mr. Cepic, so do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, will you agree with the statement of VG-13 who knew Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She knew them because she worked at Hidrogradnja. She knows everything about what was going on in the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Objection. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: He didn't -- again the question that was put to the witness again mentioned the witness rather than just the proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you recall any detail at all which would help us identify that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Which person do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The person who introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how can I testify about that? I only know about Sredoje and Milan. I only know about the two of them, so I can't testify about anyone else being there since I only know about them. I will not be testifying about persons I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you recall him being stout or skinny? You said that he was shorter than Milan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police officers had never been skinny, if he was on the police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This is your assumption. This is not your direct knowledge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look at him to see if he was skinny or stout.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the microphones in the courtroom please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did he have a cap on or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, both of them didn't have -- or either of them didn't have any caps. I heard them introduce themselves, and then when they were taking valuables from us, gold and money, I saw that they didn't have any caps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did any of them wear a mask over their face or a stocking or something of the sort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, not when I saw them. As for when they got in there, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Since they didn't have a cap, either of them, do you perhaps recall what sort of hair they had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know anything about that. You're asking me too much. Perhaps they were bald, I don't know. How should I know what sort of hair they had?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, in that house were the menfolk also compelled to hand over money and jewellery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did Hasib Kurspahic also turn over his valuables? Did they take money from him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. As far as I know, all of us did. I'm not able to tell you in respect of each and every individual if they did turn over their valuables. I know that I did mine. I handed over mine and went back to where I was standing before. I don't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But Hasib was present there, was he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Of course he must have been there. All of us were there. Of course he was. Ah, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you perhaps recall if any one of these individuals had a moustache or a beard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The one who was taking us to the other room to strip us naked did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did he introduce himself to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he were here today, I would tell him, "Why don't you look at a naked balija now." That's what I would tell him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to do my best in the next ten minutes, Your Honour, maybe less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, I understand the pain you're feeling, and I'll try to take this slowly. While you were being searched, were you on the first floor of the Memic house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think that we were on the second floor. That's what it seems to me, because I recall descending the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did the room have any windows?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Up -- where do you mean, downstairs or upstairs where they were taking our money?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I meant upstairs, madam.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upstairs. Well, of course there were. Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, will you agree with me that you don't know who Sredoje Lukic is and that you're claiming that it was Sredoje Lukic because others told you to do so and because a person introduced himself as Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, don't, please don't. I didn't come here to tell lies or untruths. I would that nobody had been there, because I wouldn't be there either.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, thank you very much. I have no more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me emphasise once more that I understand the pain you've been through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We have no redirect, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: My colleague Mr. Weber will be handling the next witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Who is the witness, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Adam Weber on behalf of the Prosecution. At this time the Prosecution called VG-78.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long are you going to be, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a 92 ter witness. I anticipate finishing within the hour allowed by the Court if the Court would allow me to lead on matters that were already covered in this witness's previous testimony and statement, I believe I could efficiently go through today's proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, provided they are non-controversial and the Defence have no objections to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. And you may begin, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. May I ask the court usher to tender the witness the sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-78, you have been granted protective measures by the Trial Chamber, and we will be using a pseudonym instead of your name today throughout your testimony.
