I'm directing your attention to the sheet that appears in front of you. Could you please confirm if your name and date of birth appear on that sheet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please sign the sheet.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Where, here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Anywhere would be fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders the pseudonym sheet into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P86 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: May the court officer -- sorry. Could the court usher please hand to the witness this sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-78, you have been provided with a reference sheet which contains the names of persons you may wish to name during the course of your testimony. Could you please refrain from using those individual names and instead use the pseudonyms or numbers that appear next to those individuals' names on this sheet. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-78, what village did you live in up until June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: In the village of Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was your age in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I was 22. I was born in 1968.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you previously testify in the case of the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic on the 28th of September and 1st of October, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review that testimony in the Bosnian language before coming to court here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, pursuant to Rule 92 ter the Prosecution tenders into evidence VG-78's prior testimony in the Vasiljevic case, which is 65 ter numbers 132 and 133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 132 will become Exhibit P88; and 133, P89 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The underlying exhibits referred to and authenticated in that testimony are 65 ter numbers 130 under seal, 131 under seal and 184. The Prosecution at this time tenders those three exhibits into evidence based upon the previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the 65 ter numbers? They're not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course. The first one was 65 ter 130, which is under seal, the second one was 131 also under seal, and the last one was 184.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 130 will become Exhibit number P87 under seal. 65 ter 131 will become Exhibit P90 and 184 will become P91, all under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-78, did you also provide a statement to an ICY -- ICTY investigator on the date of the 23rd of January, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review that statement in the Bosnian language before coming to court here today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions that you were asked when you provided that statement, would you give the same answers to the Court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is that statement true and accurate to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Pursuant to Rule 92 ter, the Prosecution tenders into evidence VG-78's prior statement from the 23rd of January, 2001, which is 65 ter number 183.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P92 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the court usher please call up Exhibit P92, which is the ICTY statement and turn to e-court page 4 of both the English and the B/C/S versions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the second paragraph from the top of the page. Did you state in your ICTY statement that: "I knew Milan Lukic very well. He was born in 1967, and he was from a neighbouring village to the village where Mitar Vasiljevic came from. Both of us went to school in Prelovo. He was one grade ahead of me. After finishing 8th grade he left and moved to Serbia." Was that your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How many years did you attend school with Milan Lukic in Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Seven years.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During the course of those seven years that you attended school with Milan Lukic, where would you see him in school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I'd see him in passing in the hallways during our breaks. I'd see him among other students there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Milan Lukic outside of school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where would you see --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Around the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And where --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Around the school building with other students as he was passing by.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention now to your previous testimony that you provided to the -- to the Tribunal. Did you discuss in that testimony a particular day in June of 1992 in which you and other individuals from your village of Koritnik left Koritnik and went to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: The 14th of June, 1992. That was the date when we set out from the village of Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On the 14th of June, 1992, did you eventually go to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did you and the other members of your village go in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: We went to the Mahala neighbourhood, to the Pionirska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you went to Pionirska Street, did you go to a particular place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. We were told to go up there to be put up there, to spend the night. We were supposed to take a bus on the following day from Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you go to a particular house on Pionirska Street in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. We went where we were told to go. We were given that possibility to spend the night there and to go for Kladanj on the following day. They said that should anyone come to the house we should show them the piece of paper that they gave us where they allegedly guaranteed our safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You're referring to "we." Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: The Serbs who found the accommodation for us. Milan and Mitar Vasiljevic, the ones who put us up at that house, told us we would be spending the night in that home and leaving for Kladanj the following day. Mitar Vasiljevic gave us a piece of paper where we were allegedly guaranteed safety, where nobody was allowed to mistreat us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe this house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: It was a big house which had a small kitchen, two rooms, a corridor, and an attic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you previously testify as to what happened in this house on Pionirska Street on the 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to once you arrived at the house on Pionirska, I'd like to reference a particular portion of your previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If the court officer could please call up Exhibit P88, which is page 1287, line 20 through -- I'm sorry, line 22 through page 1288, line 3 from her previous testimony. It's e-court pages 11 and 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-78, during your previous testimony were you asked the following questions and did you provide the previous testimony: "Q. Did there come a time that afternoon that Milan Lukic arrived? "A. Yes. "Q. How many later was this in relation to the last time you saw Mitar Vasiljevic? "A. About an hour later, maybe less. I can't remember exactly. "Q. Was it still light outside or already dark? "A. It was light."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you personally see Milan Lukic when he came into the house on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you sitting or standing at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how far was Milan Lukic from you when you saw him arrive at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: About a metre and a half away. Perhaps a little more or a little less. I can't quite remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You mentioned that there was light outside. Was there visible light inside of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you see Milan Lukic's face at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you saw Milan Lukic, what was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: A camouflage. He didn't have a hat on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say "camouflage," what articles of clothing was he wearing that were camouflaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Multicoloured, the multicoloured type of clothing that the Serbs wore, the Serb soldiers. I don't remember exactly. Anyway, multicoloured clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When Milan Lukic arrived at the house on this first occasion was he with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. There were two others, but I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time when Milan Lukic entered the house were you with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. I was standing there with my sister and all my family, my mother, my brother's children and his wife, my family, my relatives from the village of Koritnik. We were all there in the house. Some of them were in the room, other -- the others were in the house because there were two rooms and a hallway and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does your sister's name appear on that sheet in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court what is her pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did VG-101 say anything to you when Milan Lukic arrived at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes, she did. She said, "Do you know who this is?" And I couldn't remember, so I asked her who it was, and she said this is Milan Lukic from the village of Prelovo who went to school the eight years of elementary school when we went to school. So she recognised him first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was there any doubt in your mind at this time that the individual that arrived at the house was Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, no. I had no doubt. When he ran into the house, he was saying something, and my sister at that point in time, as he rushed into the house, she said that that was Milan Lukic from the village of Prelovo. Trsvina or Pozdercici or some other hamlet, but anyway, from Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Milan Lukic said something. What did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. He came into the house and he said, "Your valuables, money." He said that in a very loud voice and said that if they found anybody with those things on them they would -- he would cut their fingers off.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After Milan Lukic demanded valuables and threatened to cut off people's fingers, what did he then do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: They collected up the money, and the people who were with him took the money away, and after that he recognised Jasmina Vila, and he said, "How come you're here?" And he hugged her and took her outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You've mentioned Jasmina Vila. Was she in the same room as you at the time that Milan Lukic came into the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. She was there somewhere. Whether she was in the room or in the house, but she was there anyway. She was among us in the house, there in the house with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how far were you from Milan Lukic when he walked over to Jasmina Vila?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember exactly. It was all in the house. People were moving around. You couldn't actually tell. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you give an approximation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, perhaps ten steps away, something like that. Ten steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When Milan Lukic went over to Jasmina Vila, were you able to see his face during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes. I saw him. They passed right by me, right next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic proceed to leave with Jasmina Vila?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He left the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On this first occasion that you observed Milan Lukic, approximately how much time passed between when he first arrived to when he left the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember really.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Can you approximate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you testify about another occasion that you saw Milan Lukic on the 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When was it that you saw Milan Lukic again on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I saw him in the evening when they came to tell us to go out of that house into another house, and they said we should leave our things there, and allegedly he looked through our things to check if there were any weapons or anything like that. In front of the house where the people were sent off to, to the house where they were all -- where they burnt them all. And he was moving around. Mitar was there at the door. He said, "You don't need shoes. You can go barefoot."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to a specific portion of your previous testimony regarding the second occasion that you observed Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Court officer, this is Exhibit P88 again. It's page 1290, lines 14 through 19 from her previous testimony. It's e-court page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-78, did you provide the following testimony on the 28th of September, 2001? "Q. Did you recognise any of these men? "A. I saw Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic walking between the two houses. They were not in front of this house, but I ran away together with VG-101. I hid behind the shed and then went down to a creek and through the woods, as far away as I could from the town."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you saw Milan Lukic on this second occasion when he was with Mitar Vasiljevic, approximately how far was he from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, about 30 steps away, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the lighting -- I'm sorry. What was the lighting like at that time out in front of house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, there were lights outside. In the houses you could see proper lights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What time was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 11.00 or half past 11.00, maybe 12.00. We didn't have a watch to see what the time was. Well, someone did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was Milan Lukic with anyone else at this time besides Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. There was a man standing in front of the door with a moustache. I don't know his first or last name. He was in the house and mistreated the people. He stood in front of the door. He had a moustache, and he had a battery, and he would shine the torch, actually, as people went out, but I don't know what his name was. I don't know his name or surname. I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were there any other individuals besides the individual with the moustache?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, in front of the door. One of them had a torch and would shine it at the people as they left the house and, yes, there were others, but they moved around. As the people came out of the house, they moved towards the other house, whereas this one was in front of the door. He stood in front of the door waiting for all the people to come out, the one with the moustache that I said I didn't know what he was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you saw Milan Lukic on this second occasion, what portion of him could you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, there were people going to the other house. They were standing around there, and I was behind the house, by the shed with my sister, and we went past a creek and escaped that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you saw Milan Lukic on the second occasion, could you see his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Just a little bit. His profile. Not like when I saw him in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you saw him in the house were you looking at him from straight on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-78, at this time I'd like you to take a look around the courtroom. Could you please let us know whether or not you recognise any of the individuals in this courtroom aside from myself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Milan Lukic over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: The second one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe something that he's wearing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: A white shirt and a suit. Now, whether it's blue or greenish I can't -- or grey. Yes, it's grey. I can't really tell. But the shirt's white, and he's the second one next to the first gentleman there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say the second one, are you referring to who exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, Milan Lukic over there. He's sitting there. He's got a glass in front of him and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect the identification of the accused Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's got a blue -- blue patterned tie.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Hasib Kurspahic and Edhem Kurspahic, but they're not alive. They've also died. They died after coming out of that house. They died later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are there any other individuals that you are also aware that survived the burning at that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes, yes, there are others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who are those other individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good afternoon, VG-78.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, I'd like to ask you -- I know that your statements have been introduced into evidence and your prior testimony has been introduced into evidence, but the prior testimony was from the trial of Mitar Vasiljevic and I represent Milan Lukic in this case. May I ask you some questions this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you're from the village of Koritnik. Is that where you were born and stayed there until 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at what age did you start primary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I was seven. You mean the first form? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How old was your first year of primary school? How old were you? Seven?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Seven, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that children from Rujiste went to primary school in the village of Klasnik for grades 1 through 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: They went from grade 1 to 8. The village of Prelovo, not Klasnik. That's another village. That might have been the case in Klasnik. This is Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But if I were to tell you that Milan Lukic is not from Prelovo but from Rujiste, then where would the children from Rujiste go to primary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, I did not get the translation of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that the children went to Prelovo from Zupa. That's what the villages and hamlets behind Prelovo are referred to as Zupa, but the went to Prelovo and that was up to grade 4. Other villages might have had some other school but I didn't hear that they had any primary school because the primary school was in Prelovo for all the children in the surrounding parts, both for Serbs and for Muslim children.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, how far away is the -- or isn't it true that it's ten kilometres from Klasnik to Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And isn't it true that Rujiste is 23 kilometres from your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know how far it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so if Milan were from Rujiste, wouldn't it be true that he would only go to Prelovo from grades 5 through 8?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: As far as I know, he went to Prelovo, and it's common knowledge that he went to school -- that Milan Lukic went to school in Prelovo from grade 5 -- well, if the first school was from 1 to 4, grades 1 to 4, the other one was from 1 to 8 in the village of Prelovo. So the pupils went to that school. I've never heard of this school just from grades 1 to 4 in Klasnik, Kapetanovici and so on. I lived in Visegrad for a long time but I never heard of the existence of this school anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it true that children from the village of Koritnik went to primary school in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: To Prelovo, not to Visegrad. The children from Koritnik went to school in Prelovo. And as for secondary school they went to Visegrad to attend secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Nobody --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how old is someone when they leave primary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the child, when they start school. If they start school later, then they finish later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What's -- when did you finish primary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I was 15, 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that's when you finished primary school or secondary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I hadn't completed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so when was your last year of school and where did you finish school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: In Sarajevo. I went to secondary school in Sarajevo, not in Visegrad, whereas primary school I went to Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in 1992 how old were you again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I'm -- I don't understand your question. When I set out from Koritnik or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In 1992, how old are you in June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, 22 when I left Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when did you finish school in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I didn't attend school regularly. I took my exams privately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when did you move to Sarajevo from Visegrad, in what year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How old were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: It's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How old were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was the last year you were in school anywhere in the municipality or area around Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'd -- there's an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a misstatement of her previous testimony. If counsel would like to ask her when she was -- last attended a school in Prelovo we'd have no objection, but there's the implication that she went to school in Visegrad in this question. I believe that misstates the witness's prior testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're saying that it's incorrect to say Prelovo is in the area around Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe the question is phrased in the municipality. We would agree that it's in the area around Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think it's a big issue, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, what was the last year and how old were you the last year that you attended school anywhere around Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I told you that I didn't go to school in Visegrad but in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In your village of Prelovo or in the school of -- or town of Prelovo, how old were you the last year you attended school there?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If there's going to be questions concerning this I would ask that we go into private session in order to protect this witness's identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes, private session. And that's to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, I'm going to ask you again. You were in the same house as VG-18 and 84 all evening before being removed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. Before they moved over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'm -- on the screen there is those statements that we were talking about back in 1995, and you indicated that they came to you to get information, you didn't go to them. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, did you go to the authorities to report a crime, or did you they hear that you were a witness and come to you to investigate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. They came to me. They came to my house having heard about that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how long did they stay with you? This -- this statement is three to four pages long, three pages in Bosnian. How long did they talk to you to compile this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, did they -- they bring a typewriter with them and type as you were speaking, or did they return after the meeting and show you the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No. The first time they were asking questions of me there was a teacher there, and then they came the second time, and then only those who came from The Hague Tribunal to my house had the machines with them, but not the ones who were there before.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court assistants go to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is that your signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so after interviewing you, the people that -- did you type this yourself or was it typed by an official?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I didn't type it out. It was the one who came -- the ones who came to see me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And -- and -- but you did read the statement and you signed all the pages. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And your memory should have been the most fresh as close to the incident as possible, and memory tends to fade over time. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No. My memory improved over time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true -- and I'd ask to move to page 2 of the English statement, and I think it might still be on page 2 -- yes, page 2 on both statements. Now, the only place that Milan Lukic's name appears is in the first sentence of the second paragraph on page 2. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. What is the basis?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just would ask that counsel would include in his question the other references to Milan Lukic in that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're saying there are other references to the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe it's -- six lines from the top of that paragraph there's another reference to Mr. Lukic in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour, and I'd be moving these two statements into evidence so I don't forget.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objection. We just ask that they be kept under seal because of the personal nature of the information in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will -- could I please ask counsel to switch off the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will become Exhibit number 1D35 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in this statement you make no mention of Mitar Vasiljevic being there at the end of the night. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I mentioned him as being there outside the door when he was telling us that we didn't need our shoes on, that we could go barefoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Isn't it true that in the statement of 1995 you only mention Mitar Vasiljevic as being present at the Red Cross wearing civilian clothing and giving Meho a document to show Serbian police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in this statement you did not include that he was there at 2350 hours. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, fine, but the truth is that he was. When we got to the house one of the ladies who didn't survive said, "Mitar Vasiljevic gave us a certificate." He used to work with her brother. They were good mates. Apparently we were not supposed to be afraid. She said that she was quite glad of Mitar having been there, because he was on good terms with her brother. And she also said, "Don't be afraid. We'll be the first ones to set out for Kladanj."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And also in this statement you make no mention of the robbery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I said everything the way it was, that they took money and gold -- or, rather, that first they came to pick us up and that we had left everything behind. As we moved from one house to the other we left all our belongings in the first house. Perhaps it was not recorded, but I did state that, I do recall clearly stating that they came to the house, took our valuables, gold, money, and they took Jasmina Vila away with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And -- but they didn't bother you other than taking your gold and jewellery? Did you have any gold or jewellery that was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes, I did. I had some money, and I turned everything over, the money and gold.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were you personally harmed in any other way or molested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No. No. As far as that goes, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Not that I was mistreated or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, a little -- and this house that you're in, it was just a single storey with two rooms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. It was a big house with two rooms and a hallway. There was an attic, but I don't remember if there was a bathroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was the attic finished as in people lived in the attic, or -- or was it just the first floor that people lived on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: As far as I remember, one had to go up the stairs. I don't know if it had one floor or more floors. I didn't really pay attention to that. I know that there were two rooms, a hallway, a kitchen. There was a balcony.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, you did have -- well, the first time you learned that there were survivors other than yourself was from your brother. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: In the village of Babin Potok where we fled to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is that where you saw your brother again? How much longer after the incident did you see your brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: We were in Babin Potok for 20 days. He heard that we had fled and survived, so he came to see us and to take us across the Drina to Crni Vrh, to safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is it at that reunion that he told you who had survived, and you later told the investigators in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes. We believed that we were the only ones to survive since there was no electricity in Babin Potok and it was impossible to hear the news. He told us of the persons who had survived and got out of the house, that one of them was in Gorazde, the other one in Zepa. Two or three persons were in Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did he tell you that the news of this incident was all over Muslim radio?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When you said that you couldn't hear the radio or anything, I wondered if he had heard that it was on the news.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No, he didn't hear that. How could he have?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: He couldn't listen to the radio and he couldn't get in touch with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But later on you spoke with VG-18, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I didn't. She was in Zepa and I was at Crni Vrh. We didn't see each other before 1993. It was only then that I met up with VG-18.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you discuss surviving the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you should have seen everything VG-18 saw since you were in the house all afternoon and all evening?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. Calls for speculation as to what VG-18 saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Reformulate, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You should have witnessed many of the same experiences that VG-18 had since you were in the house with her all afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, if you can't reformulate, move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When you reunited, what did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: We talked about what had happened to us. We talked about how the events unfolded, how we got to the house. She told me about the people who were burnt in the house. We talked about how we had left home, how a neighbour told us that we should move out to Kladanj, how they told us that they would accompany us there and how it all came to nothing, how we got to Pionirska Street in the Mahala neighbourhood and all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, isn't it true that you still speak with her on occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No, not really. I don't have an opportunity to see her since we are quite far apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, the next time you gave a statement was -- was 2001. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it was in 2001 that you added a -- a bit more detail. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in this statement you indicated that a Radomir Djuric came to your village sometime before you were leaving and told you that the White Eagles had arrived and you had to leave.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you had been hearing about the White Eagles for quite some time, and there were rumours that they had burned down villages, killed people, and taken girls away. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were you in the stadium, in the football stadium, when a Colonel Jovanovic --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you hear about that, when all the people were in the stadium?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I did, but I was in my village, in the village of Koritnik. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did you hear that General Jovanovic said that he controlled the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was Radomir Djuric a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes, he was, on the Serb police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were there any other Serb police officers that either escorted you or directed you away from your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: He told us that he would escort us to Visegrad and that we would be leaving by bus to Kladanj at 1200 hours. However, he did not show up on the following day when he was supposed to escort us, and we had to set out for Visegrad on our own. The Serb police force waited for us at Visegrad. They said that -- first they said that they would put us up at Bikavac and then decided to direct us to Mahala where quite a few Muslims had moved out of their homes and quite a few homes were empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so it wasn't until you were already in Mahala at the request of the police that you saw Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes. He accompanied us to the area outside the hotel -- or, rather, to Pionirska Street, and he gave a piece of paper to one man from Sase.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you get the impression that the man you knew as Mitar Vasiljevic was doing things at the direction of the police that were at the hotel in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I don't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, did Mitar seem like he was in a position of authority or that he was merely passing messages?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. He gave us the piece of paper. Where exactly he was I didn't notice. I was too frightened. I know that he handed over that piece of paper to us in the house where it said that we shouldn't be afraid. Now, whether he received orders from the Serb police, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you saw -- how many police officers were armed and outside the MUP before you moved on to the square?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: They were there. I don't remember how many. They milled around the town, and there were some outside the police station. I didn't pay special attention to that. I did see them around Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in -- when Mitar Vasiljevic and four other Serbs arrived and gave the note, did you recognise the four other Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No. I was in the house then when the people who received the note from Mitar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So they only told you that Mitar had given the note. You did not witness this exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes, yes. No, I didn't see that, but they passed it on from one to the other. That's it. Some said that Mitar worked with his brother, and so he hoped that we would go to Kladanj because Mitar knew the brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your statement of 2001, you indicated that you did see the four men that were with him and they all had camouflage uniforms. Are you saying you didn't see them now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I did because they were in front of the door. They came later when Mitar and the other people were there. And people said that they were in front of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, before it was -- when it was getting dark, there was no electricity in the home, so did you have any other way of lighting the inside of the home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No, no. It was outside. The lighting came from the street outside. That's how the house received its electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in your statement of 2001, you indicated that you knew Milan Lukic very well. He was born in 1967, and he was from a neighbouring village, but yet in your testimony today you indicated that your sister had to tell you that that was Mitar -- or excuse me, Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes, I knew him, but she said that it was Milan Lukic. Of course I knew him, and I recognised him. But when he stormed into the house and asked for valuables, money, and so on, shouting, I was afraid, and in that general commotion and fear she said it first.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yet the last time you'd really seen the Milan Lukic that you think was when you were in primary school, and he was not yet a grown man. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I don't know understand what you just said. I'm not following.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, if you're finishing primary school at 14 or 15 years of age, doesn't that mean that you actually might have been even further behind Milan Lukic if you were only one year behind him in age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I was 7th grade. He was 8th grade. My relatives went to the Prelovo primary school with him because they were the same age as him, and they remember very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He remembers them very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Prior to that night when you saw Milan Lukic in 1992, when was the last time that you had seen him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That evening when I saw him for the last time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no, before that. Before that evening, when was the last time you had seen him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw him there and then in that house. Before that I didn't see him. I don't remember, but I had heard that people were saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Never mind that. Counsel is suggesting that the last time that you saw Milan Lukic before that evening was when you were in primary school with him. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think I saw him around, but I don't remember exactly when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, she says that she might have seen him around, but she doesn't remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I guess we'll --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I think we'll have to let the answer stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I want to take you to after 11.00 p.m., after 2300 hours, and there was some commotion and everyone was woken up and asked to leave, but in your statement of 2001 you say that "some in the group said that Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic and their group were supposed to kill us all. I heard somebody from our group saying we should leave the house in a row one by one and walk to a nearby house." What do you mean by "someone in the group said that Milan Lukic and Mitar Vasiljevic were supposed to kill us all"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was it an announcement? What did you hear? Why were you leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: They took away the girls to the hotel, Milan Lukic. When we were in our village of Koritnik we heard everything. We heard what he was doing and that he was taking girls away, and I know the ones that survived. And we were afraid of that, because we didn't think he'd do anything to the women and children. However, when they turned up at that hour, that time, to separate the girls and take them to the Hotel Vilina Vlas, that's why we decided. And we were lucky to have saved our lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But isn't it true that the girls were supposed to be taken away earlier in the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes, after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And nothing happened at the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Not in the house, but the ones they set aside, separated, they said that's what would happen. So we planned to take our chances. But some of the girls told us that they took them away to the house opposite and then did what they wanted with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that -- well, what were these gentlemen wearing? What was Milan Lukic wearing? What was his ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I think he was wearing a multicoloured -- multicoloured clothing. It was a long time ago. He was wearing this clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was the main colour in this multicoloured clothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did he have anything on his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No, he didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did anyone have anything on their head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, some people did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: The one standing in front of the door with the moustache, he had something on his head, some kind of cap.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you indicated, though, that there were eight or nine Serbs, including Mitar and Milan. What about the other seven? What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: They were wearing the coloured clothes, those standing in front of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did they have any hats on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that. Some did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Anyone in the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes, Mitar Vasiljevic had a hat on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You had seen him in that hat earlier in the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes, from the hotel when he passed by the people. Whether he arrived before us or after us I don't know, but when he came to the house he was in front of the door and people were saying that that was Mitar Vasiljevic, the people who had seen him. They passed the word around.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So this was -- again, you did not have personal knowledge of who this was but this is something that someone had told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes. They told me that that was him personally, people who knew him better, the older people. They said that it was Mitar Vasiljevic bringing in the note and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it possible that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: And I knew him. He worked in Visegrad in the Panos Hotel. I saw him in town. He would be in front of the hotel and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that Mitar Vasiljevic broke his leg falling off a horse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Mitar Vasiljevic proved he was in a hospital the night of this fire would that change your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. The witness has answered the question that was posed to her directly. This calls for speculation --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a second. An objection has been raised.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That never happened. He never broke his leg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Don't answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the objection is withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You answered, "that never happened. He never broke his leg." Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Because he was there that evening and everybody saw him, and my whole family and the older people who knew him better than I did and everything. That was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, it's one thing for him to be there earlier in the afternoon in the square, but it's another thing for him to be there several hours later at the very end, and I'm asking you, are you sure, or are you just relying on what other people have told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I'm quite certain he was in front of the door as we left one by one, and when he said to a man from my village that he didn't need any shoes, that he could go barefoot, because he knew what would happen to the people. So he said, "You don't need any shoes." He told him that he could go barefoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you're saying Mitar Vasiljevic is the one that told people they didn't need their shoes or belongings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you indicate that the person you believe to be Milan Lukic at that late hour was more than 30 steps away from you as you left the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes. He was in front of that house over there where they met the people and burnt them in that house. He moved around there in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you say 30 steps, is that 30 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. I didn't count.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How many people left the house before you? Were you in the front of the line or the back of the line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No, I wasn't in front or at the back. Well, I don't remember. There were people behind me, and there were people who had gone there. How could I remember things like that with all that fear? How would you like it? How would you feel?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, what I'm getting at is that there's probably a lot of people in between you and the other house that are blocking your view, and maybe you really couldn't see the guy that was down by the house in the dark.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, we saw -- as the column was moving, they followed the people there up to the house, then they withdrew where the people were, and the moustached person was in front of the door with a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you were able to slip away and go behind the shed, how far away is that shed from the front door of the house you'd just left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: I don't remember. It was a long time ago, but it wasn't far and it wasn't near.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And wouldn't it be true that the people that were actually between you and the other house are what helped block your escape from the view of the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's how we managed to escape. Some were in front, others were behind, and when the people were waiting outside the house we managed to escape before. We didn't go to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And these same people would block your view of the house as they blocked your view from the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, we saw them. We saw them moving around amongst the people. We saw them as we were coming out. That's how we saw them. But then they went further off, because most of the people had already gone over there, but there was still some in the house left behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember what day of the week the 14th was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: The 14th? I think it was a Sunday, but I'm not quite sure. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no questions. I would just like the record to reflect that Milan Lukic is wearing a blue patterned tie today and Mr. Sredoje Lukic is wearing a red patterned tie.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what would be the basis for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just asking the record reflect that. The witness previously described in her testimony the ties that were being worn by the witnesses during her identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that would better come from the witness, not than you. You can't give that evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That evidence was already previously given.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In that regard, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The witness also identified a white shirt, and the record can reflect that Milan Lukic is wearing a blue shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just asking for the ties of whatever the record wants -- whatever they're wearing today, the record can reflect that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why don't you put it to the witness again?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd be happy to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my microphone is out of use.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't a blue shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have objection about the last words of my learned friend Mr. Weber. He's been speaking in plural, but we never heard anything related to my client. Not from direct examination, not in identification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's perfectly true, and I have suggested to him that he should put these questions to the witness again in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And all I would ask, Your Honour, is a half a dozen questions on re-cross, considering the nature of the identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's a matter I'll determine. Let's hear the questions quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-78, you've previously identified an individual in court today. Could you please point to that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: Well, the second person from this gentleman over here, the second one is Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say the second person, the second person from where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: From this first person, the second man.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you referring to individuals in what row?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Leading questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last row, up by the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: May I ask one question or two questions?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Two questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: One question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It really needs two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Two?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Two questions. I can only -- I have to preface it with one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead. Recross-examination by Mr. Alarid:

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, in your -- attached to your statement of 2001, you identified a photograph of Mitar Vasiljevic, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. That is outside the scope of redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The second question is the more important one, assuming she recalls the identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, counsel is right, counsel for the Prosecution. I would allow you to ask something that would have arisen from the re-direct exceptionally, but you are raising an entirely new matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would ask leave of the Court to do so, Your Honour, in the interests of justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just for the record, Your Honour, that we have a permanent objection about identification in courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we have noted that, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And of course, we've made the same objection. I was just going to ask her one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we have noted that. Proceed with the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Ma'am, were you ever asked to identify a photograph of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-78
utterances.text: No, never. I never had an opportunity of doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it, and you may leave now. Unless any party has a matter to raise we will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 8.50 a.m. [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
